solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Casualty cast sacrificing time for rehearsal at last

indicators.note: sacrificing one thing means giving it up, so a letter is taken out
for, after the sacrificed letter, names what is put in its place

parts.note: to cast something is to toss or throw it

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word rehearsal

explanation.surface: An injured actor's understudy is drafted in, giving up rehearsal time at the final moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty can be a loss, as in a death or something written off in battle or business.

clue.text: Black cat makes jump suddenly

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard, a large wild cat

explanation.surface: A black cat startles someone into leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce is to spring or leap up abruptly, a synonym for a sudden jump.

clue.text: Claim source of emotional stress is supporting Spurs regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after what it holds up
regularly takes every other letter of the word Spurs, here the second and fourth
the source of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: stress and tension are synonyms

explanation.surface: A football fan claims that following Tottenham Hotspur causes emotional strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. 'is supporting' works on a down clue: PR goes beneath E plus TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretension is an assertion or claim to something, as in having pretensions to the throne.

clue.text: Dedicated bishop inside recently after ignoring fine

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other
ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: of late is a phrase meaning recently
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A devoted bishop has lately gone unpunished by a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes F from OF LATE to leave OLATE, and B goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a person dedicated to religious life, so as an adjective it means consecrated or devoted.

clue.text: Embracing Welsh day of celebration, American and Italian served up dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the whole is read upwards, that is backwards
embracing means holding something within, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: St David's Day, the Welsh national day, falls on 1 March, written I MAR

explanation.surface: An American and an Italian serve a pudding at a St David's Day party.
explanation.walkthrough: St David, patron saint of Wales, has his day on 1 March, written I MAR. 'Embracing' wraps the outer pair round it; 'served up' reads USIMARIT upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, an example of a dessert.

clue.text: Couple in conference, perhaps overheard

indicators.note: overheard means the word is heard spoken, so a soundalike is entered

parts.note: Conference is a popular variety of pear, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Two people at a conference might be overheard talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a well-known British variety of pear.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple and a pair both mean two things or people together.

clue.text: Separate food hotel dumped on island

indicators.note: dumped means thrown away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers on a Greek island ditch the hotel and its food to eat separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct, separate and not joined to others.

clue.text: Person granted exclusive marketing concession, the fifth such one?

parts.note: such one refers back to the exclusive marketing concession, which is a franchise
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A trader with sole selling rights wonders whether they hold the fifth such licence.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 9,1 the answer reads as franchise number E, the fifth in a lettered series.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchisee is the holder of a licence to trade under another company's brand in an area.

clue.text: Cologne's common accompaniment, pronounced fragrance?

indicators.note: pronounced means the phrase is said aloud and a soundalike entered

parts.note: the words usually preceding Cologne are eau de, as in eau de Cologne

explanation.surface: A strong scent is the usual partner of a cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne here is the German city, as in eau de Cologne; the French 'eau de' said aloud resembles O DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, and a fragrance is a pleasant smell or scent.

clue.text: Officer support for late individual carrying kit to attend active duty

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the frame goes round the rest

parts.note: a bier is the stand on which a dead person's coffin rests

indicators.note: to attend means to go alongside, so the two pieces sit together

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment or kit
AD is the abbreviation for active duty

explanation.surface: An officer carries kit while accompanying a dead comrade on active service.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, commanding a brigade, ranking above colonel.

clue.text: Singer, performer contracted to go west touring North America

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reversed piece encloses the other
in an across clue going west means reading right to left, backwards
contracted means shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: an artist is a performer

explanation.surface: A singer signed up to tour American venues out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' leaves ARTIS, 'to go west' turns that into SITRA, and 'touring' puts it round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the famous American crooner, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Moor, say, a vessel having day on board

indicators.note: having, with on board, means the vessel holds the day inside
on board means carried inside the vessel, so the day sits within

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
FRI is short for Friday, a day

explanation.surface: A sailor from Morocco boards a ship for a day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: a Moor is a person from north-west Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moors were Muslim people of north-west Africa, so a Moor is one example of an African.

clue.text: Small bird's tail

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A little bird's tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship, and tail also means the hind end.

clue.text: Rock album, it's including work of unsatisfactory standard

indicators.note: including means holding the other piece inside
rock means shake up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A rock record, including a particular track, is not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre but signals the anagram, which gives SUBTIMAL; 'including' then sets the work inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Suboptimal means falling short of the best possible, hence below an acceptable level.

clue.text: Taking gamble, Hazel and I developed new line in London

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the anagram wraps round the gamble
developed means changed or evolved, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: Hazel and I took a punt and launched a new London venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' gives ELIZAH, which 'Taking' wraps round the gamble. The Elizabeth line is a London rail line opened in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabeth line is the recently opened cross-London railway named after the late Queen.

clue.text: England fan hoping all fans cheer, essentially …

indicators.note: fans out means spreads, so the letters are rearranged
essentially points to the central letter of the word cheer

explanation.surface: An England supporter wishes every supporter would cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like a noun for supporters but signals the anagram, giving ANGLOPHIL; 'essentially' supplies E from the heart of cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anglophile is a foreign admirer of England and its culture, an England lover.

clue.text: Belgium's grudges about habits of Australian male sunbathers?

indicators.note: about means turned around or scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about how sunbathers dress in Australia, blamed on the Belgians.
explanation.walkthrough: Budgie smugglers is Australian slang for tight men's swimming briefs; 'habits' means garments, as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits are clothing, and this slang name for tight trunks comes from Australian beaches.

clue.text: … substitute messes it up, edgy about defending

indicators.note: about means the concealed letters are read the other way round
defending means guarding something held within these clue words

explanation.surface: A stand-in player blunders, nervous about defending.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in 'messES IT UP EDgy', read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to stand in for someone, acting as their substitute.

clue.text: Expats ultimately approving of congregating together in colonies

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Expats

parts.note: warming to something means coming to approve of it

explanation.surface: British expats eventually take to life in the colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming describes bees or insects massing in great numbers, gathering as a colony does.

clue.text: Conceited types pay quick visit to Leno's house?

parts.note: to pop in is to pay a short call
Jay Leno is a US talk-show host, so his house is Jay's

explanation.surface: Vain celebrities drop by a famous comedian's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, foppish, self-important person, so these are vain or conceited sorts.

clue.text: Hospital staff member from Barbados is terrific

indicators.note: from means taken out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hospital worker from the Caribbean is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a sister is a senior nurse, a member of a hospital's staff.

clue.text: Duck approaching lake given peeled fruit

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

indicators.note: peeled means the outer layers are stripped, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A duck by a lake is offered some peeled fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small oily stone fruit of the Mediterranean olive tree.

clue.text: Shut up adolescent losing vacuous argument

indicators.note: losing means dropping some letters

parts.note: adolescent behaviour is immature

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, leaving only the outside letters of argument

explanation.surface: A teenager is told to be quiet, having lost a pointless row.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure is to wall in or confine someone, as a prisoner is shut up in a cell.

clue.text: Temporary signs, they're oddly disregarded before motorway turning

indicators.note: with the odd letters ignored, only the even ones of these words remain
turning means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: Temporary road signs get ignored before a motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, written MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means provisional, holding the place for a while until something permanent arrives.

clue.text: Complete degree

definitions.meaning: a degree or level in a hierarchy, a grade

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means utter as an adjective, and a rank is a position or grade on a scale.

clue.text: Office workers with mediocre investment in retirement plans

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing, going backwards, so the whole is reversed
investment means putting one piece inside another

parts.note: secs is short for secretaries, office workers
meh is a slang word for mediocre or unimpressive

explanation.surface: Office staff with lacklustre pension investments make plans for retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' gives SEMEHCS, which 'in retirement' reverses. Meh is informal slang for unimpressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemes are systematic plans or arrangements for achieving something.

clue.text: Knocked back Calvados half-cut, or something fizzy instead?

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, read in reverse
half-cut means losing the first half of the word Calvados

explanation.surface: Having downed apple brandy and got tipsy, someone might switch to a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk; here it cuts CALV off. Calvados is French apple brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated, so it is an alternative fizzy drink.

clue.text: Idiot at one point pens article, generating correspondence

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: pens means encloses, holding the article inside

parts.note: once means at one time or point in the past
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fool at some stage writes a piece that provokes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is a matching or likeness of vowel sounds, a correspondence in sound.

clue.text: Sensational attraction briefly reaching papers

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing a final letter

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A sensational draw is about to hit the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking and vividly sensational, as in lurid tabloid headlines.
